From: Laura Jenkins <laura.jenkins@auroramed.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data erase workflow — can you map to SIG/CAIQ controls?

Irene,

Quick question from our security team — we’re finalizing the audit packet and need a short mapping of Redwood’s customer-scoped erase workflow to SIG/CAIQ controls. Specifically:

- How do you handle tenant-scoped debug traces that may contain PHI in ephemeral session logs? (we need steps for identification, extraction, and deletion)
- What is the verified delete path and proof-of-delete evidence your team can provide that will satisfy our SOC 2 reviewer?
- Do you offer a customer-requested immediate purge (beyond the standard TTL) and, if so, what are the SLAs and impacts on other customers’ telemetry?

We are trying to avoid a formal escape clause in the contract, but we will need a one-page overview + any artifacts we can point our auditor to. Can Aaron (copied) include any specific evidence format he prefers?

Thanks — looking to get this to audit by EOD next week.

—Laura Jenkins
Director, InfoSec
Aurora Medical

Attachment: audit-questionnaire-aurora-1025.xlsx (spreadsheet with auditor questions)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Jenkins <laura.jenkins@auroramed.com>
Cc: Aaron Miles <aaron.miles@auditpath.io>
Date: 2026-10-25T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data erase workflow — can you map to SIG/CAIQ controls?

Laura — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I’ll follow up with artifacts and a draft one-page mapping.

- Tenant-scoped debug traces: our platform segregates per-tenant logs at ingestion. For ephemeral session traces that may contain PHI we have an automated classification pass (PII/PHI regex + model-based classifier) run before tiering. Identified items are labeled and written to an encrypted, tenant-scoped debug bucket flagged for retention policy processing.

- Verified delete path: For a customer-requested purge we initiate a three-phase process: (1) identification & tag validation, (2) orchestrated deletion from hot stores + KV cache eviction, (3) deletion from cold snapshots and metadata tombstoning. Each step emits an immutable audit event (timestamp, operator, job id). We can provide a manifest (CSV) of the objects removed and a signed deletion statement for SOC 2 evidence.

- Immediate purge SLA: standard turnaround is 72 hours for large-volume purges; we offer an expedited 24-hour SLA for critical requests (requires approval by Redwood Security and may incur operational fees). Expedited purges are tenant-scoped and do not impact other tenants — we perform isolated jobs, but we do pause any cross-tenant debug aggregation for the duration to avoid accidental reindexing.

We have internal templates for the evidence: signed deletion statement, manifest, and a verifiable log-of-operations (with SHA256 hashes). I’ll attach the SIG/CAIQ crosswalk and one-page workflow draft shortly.

Linked attachments I will send in the next message: redwood_sig_caiq_evidence_v2.pdf (evidence pack), aurora_erase-runbook-draft.md (customer-facing runbook). If Aaron has a preferred format for the manifest, please flag it.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none in this message

Aaron prefers a CSV with columns: object_key, tenant_id, detected_label, stored_at, sha256, deleted_at, deletion_job_id.

Timeline: can we deliver the one-page mapping + sample manifest by tomorrow EOD? Laura is pushing audit to next week.

Thanks — treat as high priority; include attachments in the reply.

—Irene
